quote: Create your first Turso Cloud database

text: Run a local database as a single file with no server process required
quote: local database file, no server needed (recommended)

text: Create a copy-on-write branch for development/testing without touching the original database
quote: Branches are useful for development and testing, because they allow you to make changes to the database without affecting the original database.

text: Point-in-time recovery restores a database to a specific past moment, e.g. after an accidental drop
quote: PITR allows you to restore a database to a specific point in time. This is useful for recovering from user errors, such as dropping a table by mistake.

text: Embedded Replicas serve reads from a local file in microseconds while writes sync to a cloud primary
quote: Embedded Replicas keep a local read replica of a Turso Cloud database: reads run locally from the file in microseconds, and writes are sent to the cloud primary and then reflected back to the replica.

text: Native vector search built into the database; store embeddings alongside relational data with no extensions
quote: Turso supports vector search as a native feature — no extensions required.

text: SDK exposes push() and pull() calls to sync a local embedded replica with the cloud database
quote: push() sends your changes to the cloud. pull() brings remote changes down.

text: Provision a dedicated, isolated SQLite database per user or AI agent, created/token-scoped/torn down via API
quote: Provision a dedicated database per user or per AI agent. Each entity gets its own isolated SQLite database that you create, token-scope, and tear down via the API.

text: MCP-capable agents can manage the Turso Cloud account (orgs, databases, groups) and run SQL without copying an API token
quote: Connect any MCP-capable AI agent and it can manage your Turso Cloud account — organizations, databases, groups — and run SQL, on your behalf... There’s no API token to copy or paste.

text: Documented 99.999999999% durability with sub-10ms latency SLA
Automate branch creation to spin up a new database per pull request from CI

text: Spin up thousands or millions of isolated databases programmatically as a core architectural feature
quote: Spin up thousands or millions of isolated databases programmatically, each with its own boundary. Not a workaround. The architecture.

text: Official SDKs available for TypeScript, Python, Rust, and Go
quote: SQLite-compatible. SDKs in TypeScript, Python, Rust, and Go. Self-serve from signup to production.

text: Fully backwards-compatible with SQLite
quote: Fully backwards compatible with SQLite, but built for the next generation

text: CLI command creates a new database directly (turso db create)

text: Multiple writers can write concurrently with zero conflicts and no locking
quote: Multiple writers, zero conflicts, without locking

text: Pro/Enterprise customers can bring their own S3 / S3-express buckets so data stays in their infrastructure
quote: Pro and Enterprise customers can use their own S3 / S3-express buckets, guaranteeing that data lives inside their infrastructure.

text: Per-database encryption with customer-held keys and bring-your-own-cloud deployment for controlled data residency
